title: Atomic model switchover protocol — design notes
content:
Context and intent:
This session captured architecture review notes for a small-but-critical piece of platform infra: an atomic switchover protocol for model artifact migrations across serving clusters. Goal: enable zero-or-minimal-downtime model version swaps (hosted and Dedicated), provide clear rollback semantics, and preserve per-tenant consistency guarantees while avoiding long blocking pauses or full-cluster drains.

Problem statement:
- We deploy model artifacts (large files, quantized bundles) to a mix of hot/edge nodes and dedicated pools.
- Replacing a model version can cause: cold starts, long cache warming, mixed-version inference results, and short windows where some requests hit new model and others old (inconsistent outputs for a conversation).
- We need a reproducible, observable, and auditable protocol that minimizes user-facing regressions and supports quick rollbacks.

High-level constraints:
- Target SLO: < 99.9% successful inference without error spikes during migration windows (short-lived regressions allowed but measured).
- No global stop-the-world: avoid draining full clusters for >30s.
- Support partial rollouts (canary by tenant, region, or capacity tier).
- Work with private deployments where networking may be slower.
- Artifacts are signed; integrity checks must run pre-commit.

Candidate approaches considered:
1) Full rolling restart (naive): sequentially restart nodes with new model.
   - Pros: simple, ensures single-version per node.
   - Cons: long tail latency, wide variability, not atomic, poor for large fleets.
2) Load-balancer atomic flip after pre-warm (two-phase): push artifacts to all nodes, warm caches, then flip routing table key globally to new model id.
   - Pros: near-atomic switch, reduced per-request variability.
   - Cons: requires reliable readiness signals and careful coordination; risk of partial visibility if some nodes fail readiness checks after flip.
3) Canary + gradual traffic shift: route small % of traffic then increase.
   - Pros: fault isolation, data-driven.
   - Cons: not atomic; conversation-level consistency can still be violated.
4) Transactional model-migration protocol (chosen hybrid): a prepare/transfer/validate/commit/abort protocol using per-tenant pinning tokens and per-node readiness handshake.
   - Pros: gives strong commit point, supports rollback, composable with canaries.
   - Cons: more complex control plane and state to manage.

Design: "Prepare/Transfer/Validate/Commit" (PTVC) protocol
- Overview:
  1) Prepare: Controller computes switchover plan (target nodes, model manifest, checksums, rollout policy). Create a migration record with UUID and signed manifest.
  2) Transfer: Push artifact to target nodes (streaming + chunk checks). Nodes store artifact in a staging area (not yet active). Each node verifies signature and checksum and reports STAGED.
  3) Validate (warm + smoke): Controller issues a "warm-and-validate" request to staged nodes with representative warm-up prompts (from curated set / tenant-specified probes). Nodes run warmup, populate KV caches, run smoke inference locally, and report METRICS (p95 latency, memory use, smoke result hash).
  4) Commit barrier: After a configurable quorum of nodes report GREEN (metrics within thresholds), controller issues COMMIT token.
  5) Atomic switch: Routing layer (model-id->node map) is updated using a single atomic operation keyed by migration UUID. Model routing middleware checks migration token per-request; if token matches committed UUID, it routes to staged path.
  6) Post-commit observation window: Monitor for quality regressions. If alarms fire, controller can issue ABORT which triggers fallback routing to previous model id and automatic drain of staged artifacts.

Key protocol details:
- Readiness quorum: for large clusters use quorum=majority; for tenant-isolated dedicated pools quorum=100% of assigned nodes.
- Timeouts: stages have tunable timeouts (transfer 10m, validate 5m, commit window 2m).
- Idempotency: every step is idempotent and uses migration UUID + node-id to dedupe.
- Node state machine: NOT_PRESENT -> STAGED -> WARMED -> COMMITTED -> ACTIVE -> ROLLBACK_PENDING -> CLEANUP.
- Routing update: routing tables are versioned and signed; we use a single-match update at the controller to swap model id mapping. The router applies update atomically by swapping pointer to new-model UUID.
- Conversation pinning: active conversations are pinned to model version at start of session. New sessions after commit get new model; long-lived sessions optionally can be opted-in to migrate mid-conversation (configurable).
- Integrity & audit: manifest includes artifact checksum, signature, build metadata. All state transitions are logged to audit stream.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- We prioritize a strong, observable commit point to give product teams confidence in rollouts. The atomic routing pointer swap means end-users see a clear cutover for new sessions.
- Conversation-level strong consistency would require draining active sessions or live-migrating KV caches; that complexity is deferred. Instead, we pin sessions to versions by default and provide an opt-in live-migration API (future work).
- We accept the complexity of a controller-driven protocol because it enables deterministic rollback and mitigates noisy neighbor effects during warmups.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Node fails to STAGED: controller retries transfer, if repeated failures exceed threshold the node is removed from quorum calculation and alert fired.
- Post-commit latency spike: automated alarm -> controller triggers ABORT or fallback policy (route a % to previous model while investigation happens).
- Partial commit visibility (some routers not updated): routers pull signed routing pointers periodically; controller pushes a signed notification to expedite but we tolerate eventual convergence within <5s in-hosted deployments, configurable in Private deployments.
- Artifact corruption during transfer: rejected by checksum/signature verification; node reports ERROR and stays NOT_PRESENT.

Operational observability requirements:
- Per-migration dashboard: progress, percent-staged, warmup metrics distribution, smoke test hashes, commit status, audit events.
- Migration traces linked to tenant id and model UUID.
- Automated regression detection: token-level quality checks comparing sampled outputs vs baseline prompt set.

Security and compliance notes:
- All artifacts signed with company KMS keys. Controller verifies signatures before instructing nodes to stage.
- For Private deployments, controller operates in a customer VPC via an agent; migration commands are encrypted and attest keys are exchanged during initial agent bootstrap.

Open questions / things to decide in follow-ups:
- Thresholds for warmup metrics (what is acceptable p95 delta vs baseline?). Action: Priya to propose thresholds by 2024-11-12.
- Conversation live-migration strategy (KV replay vs dual-execution). Action: Diego to prototype a KV-prefetch shim in a spike (2w).
- Telemetry cost tradeoff: how much warmup sampling is acceptable for large fleets. Action: Liam to model cost/benefit for a 1000-node deployment.
- Should we support a manual-commit mode for enterprise customers who demand human sign-off? Proposal: controller supports manual-approval flag; need audit UX in Console.

Action items (owners):
- Priya Patel: Draft warmup metric thresholds and smoke-test suite (due 2024-11-12).
- Diego Morales: Spike a KV-prefetch shim for conversation live-migration (2-week spike starting 2024-11-11).
- Liam O'Connor: Cost model for warmup traffic at scale and config knobs (due 2024-11-18).
- SRE Team: Define SLO alerting playbook for migration regressions + runbook for abort scenarios (due 2024-11-15).
- Ava Chen: Update controller state diagram and add migration audit events to the observability plan (due 2024-11-14).

Decisions made in this review:
- Adopt PTVC protocol as canonical migration flow for model artifact swaps (agreed).
- Use signed manifests + migration UUIDs for idempotency & audit (agreed).
- Default behavior: conversation pinning to model version; live-migration opt-in as a future opt-in capability (agreed).

Notes from attendees:
- Diego: emphasize staging storage should be configurable per-deployment because some private clusters have small staging disk.
- Priya: smoke-test suite should include small adversarial prompts to catch deterministic regressions.
- Liam: recommendation to allow per-migration throttles to avoid saturating network during transfer.

Next steps:
- Iterate on the proposal doc with thresholds and runbook additions. Prepare demo for cross-team review on 2024-11-20.
